analysis.title: The Blue Morning After: State-by-State Election Scorecard
key_insights: Democrats swept the 2026 midterms. The biggest surprise was Texas voting Democratic by a wide margin, which Jefferies says threatens the outlook for data center development in the state with the most planned data center capacity.

Jefferies expects an AI and data center unwind. Winners are clean energy (especially high-short-interest, unprofitable names), NEE, DUK and defensive AWK, ED and gas LDCs. Laggards are PNW, CNP, SO, AEP, the IPPs NRG, VST and TLN, EPCs and gas midstream.

Jefferies moves NXT (Nextpower) to its Franchise Pick among Buys and expects the rally in the most shorted clean energy names to continue. It is not convinced meaningful national or state clean energy reform will pass.

Texas Democrats won governor (Hinojosa), lieutenant governor (Goodwin), U.S. Senate (Talarico) and Railroad Commission (Rosenthal). Both the governor and lieutenant governor back pausing new data centers, making large-load cost allocation, tax treatment and permitting timelines the main risks for CNP, SRE and AEP.
CNP has about 80% of its rate base in Texas and trades at about a 12% premium to the group. Jefferies calls it clearly worse off because the expected post-election pivot to offense is delayed.

Democrats flipped the Georgia PSC to 3-2 ahead of Georgia Power's expected 2028 filing for 2029 rates. Georgia Power is about 60% of SO earnings. A forecast ~$950m/yr of large-load customer benefit gives SO a path to flat or lower rates.

PNW has the cleanest downside on Arizona concentration. Democrats Pratte and Hill led the ACC race (not yet called), which would leave PNW with two of three proven formula votes. Jefferies' downside case for PNW is about $98.

Democrats flipped the Pennsylvania State Senate 27-23, giving them a trifecta with Gov. Shapiro. Jefferies sees PPL underperforming most on direct PA exposure and EXC as most directly consequential given its forthcoming PA rate case. AWK, WTRG, UGI and FE are secondary exposures.

AEP is the catch-all laggard among large caps. Large-load pushback could spread to transmission, the center of its growth thesis, and weaker shares make equity funding more dilutive. Its approved Ohio tariff gives some protection.

EPCs are exposed in a broad tech and data center selloff because of Texas exposure. PWR has the best execution but high beta and a premium valuation, and the 765-kV opportunity becomes less certain if Texas permitting slows.

NEE gets a win-win: Donalds' Florida win removes the ROE cap and hyperscale moratorium risk at FPL, and a Democratic Congress improves the federal outlook for restoring wind and solar tax credits. DUK benefits as Florida risk clears.
Central U.S. utilities (AEE, LNT, EVRG, BKH, NWE) and ETR, MDU should hold up relatively well on intact regulatory frameworks and limited data center exposure.

Democrats won the House and flipped seven Senate seats. Jefferies lowers its odds of a 2026 lame-duck permitting deal and is cautious on midstream names KMI and WMB. It sees a federal ratepayer protection bill in 2027 as more likely.

Data centers are now a bipartisan affordability issue. Candidates in both parties converged on cost-causer-pays in OH, GA, MI, WI, IA and TX, and Jefferies expects state legislatures to be the biggest unknown for anti-data center efforts in 2027.

Overnight, AI and data center names sold off (CoreWeave -7%, Oracle -4% per CNBC). Premarket, NEE was +2.4% and XLU +0.5%, while SRE was -2.9% and VST -2.4%. Jefferies expects defensives without data center exposure to hold up better until the 2027 sessions.

risk_factors: Texas, Ohio, Georgia, Michigan and Wisconsin Democratic governors could pause or tighten data center approvals, slowing load conversion.
State legislatures in 2027 are the biggest unknown for anti-data center legislation, and Virginia moratorium bills are advancing.
Lame-duck permitting reform odds fall, negative for gas midstream and EPCs.
Several races remain uncalled (Arizona ACC, Kansas governor, Mississippi and Alaska Senate), and vote shares are the latest reported counts, not final.
Pragmatic governors may announce data center policies as soon as 1Q27, and the market reaction could be sharply negative first.
Higher equity issuance risk for utilities with weaker shares, including AEP.
vol_and_positioning: Before the vote, investors' willingness to take risk was arguably as low as during COVID, per Jefferies, which had expected the anti-AI trade (ED, AWK) to fade after the election.
Jefferies expects the rally in the most shorted clean energy names to continue given the scale of the Democratic win.
Index futures turned positive by early morning even as AI and data center names sold off overnight.
geopolitical: Democrats won the House (CBS estimate up to ~259 seats, final count pending) and the Senate, with seven Republican-held seats flipped: TX, NC, SC, OH, KS, IA and ME.
Mississippi and Alaska Senate races remain too close to call.
Democratic governors flipped or won in TX, GA, OH, NV, MI, WI and IA, many with data center pause or cost-causer-pays positions.
Virginia data center moratorium bills are advancing ahead of the January 13 legislative session.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand moves right, not away. New Democratic governors look pragmatic, with announcements possible from 1Q27, and existing queues and approved tariffs insulate names like AEP and DTE.
tension_points.bear_case: Democratic governors in TX, GA, OH, NV, MI, WI and IA back pauses or cost-causer-pays, and state legislatures could push anti-data center efforts in 2027, pressuring the 30-60 GW/year deployment goal.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Statements and actions from the new Texas governor and other state legislatures in the 2027 sessions, with possible announcements as soon as 1Q27.

tension_points.bull_case: If Thompson recovers in late counts, PNW keeps three proven formula votes, supporting the 10% formula premium on APS.
tension_points.bear_case: If Thompson loses, PNW has two of three proven formula votes through rehearing and the first annual reset, the core of the ~$98 downside case.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Late vote counts in the ACC race, and the December vote on APS's formula order by the sitting commission.

tension_points.bull_case: Split control had looked most conducive to a deal, with odds discussed at 50-60% in a Politico webinar.
tension_points.bear_case: With Democrats taking both chambers in January, they have less incentive to compromise, so Jefferies lowers its odds of a 2026 deal.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A bipartisan permitting bill reaching a vote in the lame-duck session.
